property_summary: For any actor and any deposited amount, after a successful withdraw the actor's credited balance is zero; the mutant never zeroes balances, so balances(actor) stays nonzero.

Invariant: during any reentrant re-entry triggered by withdraw, the caller's balance getter still reports the full pre-withdraw balance (checks-effects-interactions); the mutant zeroes the balance before the external call, so a reentrant observer reads 0.

Any address that has deposited and successfully withdrawn can withdraw again successfully (the reentrancy lock is released after each call), and the buggy mutant keeps the lock set forever so the second withdraw reverts and the deposited balance remains stuck.

After any address has successfully withdrawn, a subsequent withdraw from that address also succeeds (the reentrancy lock is released after each call); the mutant keeps the lock set forever so the second withdraw reverts while the first succeeded.

property_summary: For any inputs, after any successful withdraw the reentrancy lock is released so a later withdraw from a different address (even with zero balance) still succeeds; the mutant leaves the lock set forever, so that later withdraw reverts.

Rule: a re-entrant withdraw attempt during withdraw() must be blocked by the lock, so after an attacker's withdraw attempt completes (or reverts), the recorded balance is preserved (P: balances stay d); with the lock-entry removed (M), the re-entrant call succeeds and drains and zeroes the balance, breaking the rule.

property_summary: For any deposit amount d backed by contract funds, a single withdraw may pay out at most the caller's recorded balance: after a withdraw-driven payout, address(c).balance must remain >= (preBalance - d); removing the lock's reentrancy entry lets a re-entrant attacker withdraw twice, draining to preBalance - 2d and violating the rule.

For any deposited amount, a withdraw attempt by the depositor either fully reverts (leaving balances[depositor] unchanged) or pays out exactly once and zeroes it, so the final recorded balance is always either intact-and-refunded-or-once-spent — under P the re-entrant nested withdraw reverts against the lock so the outer withdraw reverts and balances[attacker] stays at the deposited amount, while M's disabled lock lets the re-entrant call succeed and zero the balance.
